title: Xero API: Setup, Authentication and Limits (2026)
summary: Xero API is an OAuth 2.0 REST API you can wire up by hand or through workflow tools. Understand the API limits that caused a real invoice sync to fail.
body_markdown:
## Running a Xero sync with Activepieces


Activepieces, an open-source automation platform, can host the heartbeat and the alert as one scheduled flow with a managed Xero connection. The person paged at 2am then inherits a visible run history instead of a script nobody remembers writing.


Describe that heartbeat and alert in the built-in chat and Activepieces builds and publishes the flow, the same artifact a builder would have wired up by hand.


Because it runs under the platform's RBAC, audit logs and run traces like any human-built flow, the person paged at 2am can open the run and read what happened, with no certification needed to follow it. You don't hire for this, you describe it.


### What the Xero integration covers


Xero has its own integration, one of the 742 in the Activepieces open source monorepo, because each service is packaged separately. You authorise it once, and the platform stores the connection and handles the OAuth token refresh that otherwise lives in your own code.


What changes is ownership: the expiry that silently kills a hand-built sync becomes the platform's job, and the connection's a named object an owner can inspect, reconnect or revoke.


Not the whole API, though: the integration exposes a set of Xero actions and triggers. Check the current integration against your needed endpoints before committing, because anything outside it's your problem.


### Retries, schedules and failure alerts


A schedule trigger starts the flow, the Xero integration does the work, and a failed step can route to a branch that notifies a person. Per-step retry behaviour and the run log are what make this auditable.


You can open a failed run and see which step broke and with what input, rather than reconstructing it from a log line.


What to take from it is that the failure path is part of the flow, not an afterthought bolted on after the first outage.


Rate-limit and tier rules still apply to you. The platform doesn't change what Xero allows, so design the schedule and batch sizes around those limits and confirm in the run trace that a throttled call's retried rather than dropped.


The alert branch should name an owner, not a channel nobody reads. That's the same ownership question the heartbeat answered, now answered inside the flow.


### When to call the API directly instead


Write code when the endpoint you need isn't in the integration, or when volume makes a step-by-step flow the wrong tool.


When Xero has no integration for an endpoint you need, Activepieces lets you generate one with AI and add it privately to your own instance.


That's the dashed box in the diagram, and you then own that integration's error handling and its respect for Xero's limits. Flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, so the ceiling you design around is Xero's quota, not a count of flows.


If most of your sync lives in that box, the platform's adding a layer rather than removing work. A purpose-built service with its own monitoring is the more honest choice.


Confirm the Xero actions available today against the integration's source in the open monorepo, where all 742 integrations are listed, before relying on it, so individual integrations may have diverged from current practice.
